title: A stack class
description:
Write a `Stack` class that throws helpful errors.

```
const s = new Stack(2);
s.push(1); s.push(2);
s.push(3)    // throws Error: Stack is full (2 items)
s.pop()      // 2
s.peek()     // 1
s.size       // 1
new Stack().pop()  // throws Error: Stack is empty
```
hints: `get size() { return this.#items.length; }` makes `s.size` work without brackets.
requirements: A `size` property that reads the current count (a getter is fine, or keep a field up to date).
Keep the items in a private field (`#items`).
`pop` and `peek` on an empty stack throw `Error("Stack is empty")`.
stretch: Use the stack to check whether brackets in a string like `"(a[b]{c})"` are balanced.
